scope: Prayer blocks 1, 3 and 5 of scan 8 only. This is not approval of the whole scan, the batch, the heading or citation lines, the encoding, or any export.

findings.occurrence: only occurrence of הַשָּׁמַיִם in 'כִּימֵי הַשָּׁמַיִם עַל־הָאָרֶץ' (Deut 11:21; block 3 has an earlier, separate אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ at word 44)
findings.issue: The candidate adds U+0596 tipcha on מ (host_index 2) on top of the pashta pair on מ and ם already settled in s8_image_adjudications.json. A tipcha and a pashta can't both stand in one word. The provenance file reports conflicts: [], so its check missed this.
findings.proposed_correction: Remove U+0596 and keep the settled form הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙. The settled pashta marks are not reopened.
findings.image_region: s8-band3.png, about y 95–165, x 330–620 (the 'כִּימֵי הַשָּׁמַיִם' line); the same line is near the bottom of s8-band2.png

findings.issue: The added U+05A5 merkha on מ is the conjunctive that normally comes before a tipcha. With the settled pashta on the next word, a different conjunctive would normally come first. I can't see the glyph under the מ clearly enough to decide.
findings.proposed_correction: Treat as tentative and don't approve it. Check it in a tight crop.

findings.issue: These added marks sit below the letters. In the bands I can see that something is printed in most of these places, but I can't identify the glyph (munach, merkha, tipcha, darga, tevir, etnachta, mahpakh or meteg), and some metegs may be missing from the print entirely. Mechanically, each one is on the letter the provenance names. None of them is image-confirmed, and none should be approved to complete the set.
findings.image_region: Crop each line of text separately, under the baseline, at 3–4× the page scan: block 3 lines 1–5 are in s8-band1.png at about y 510–870; lines 4–16 are in s8-band2.png at about y 30–890; block 5 is in s8-band3.png at about y 180–450.

findings.issue: These added zaqef qatan, revia and geresh marks sit above the line. I can see a mark above the letter in these places, but I can't tell single dots (revia) from double dots (zaqef), and I can't separate them from nearby holam dots.

block5: 24 אֹת֗וֹ (revia, next to the holam male)

findings.proposed_correction: Treat as tentative until a tight crop shows how many dots there are.

findings.issue: For these added marks, a mark of the matching kind is visible in the right place. This covers only these marks, not whole words.
There may be a small vertical stroke under the first ו, which would be a meteg like the one in word 51 וַֽאֲבַדְתֶּ֣ם. I can't confirm it.
findings.proposed_correction: None for now. If a crop shows a meteg, the form would be וַֽעֲבַדְתֶּם֙.

findings.issue: The block 1 text is identical in the baseline and the candidate. In s8-band1 the mark below this word looks like it sits under ב/ר rather than under the last letter ת, and its shape is unclear. If questions 870–877 settled this word, ignore this item.
findings.proposed_correction: None proposed. Check it in a crop.

findings.issue: The image shows one printed dot over the consonantal vav in both occurrences. Whether it is encoded as U+05B9 (primary, kept) or U+05BA (secondary) can't be read from the image. The two codepoints don't stand for different printed dots, so the choice doesn't affect how faithfully the printed mark is reproduced. Unicode recommends U+05BA for a consonantal vav with holam, so this is a pending encoding or rendering decision, outside this review.

I counted all 127 provenance entries by hand (101 in block 3, 26 in block 5), treating maqaf-joined words as one word and counting only consonants for host_index. Every entry lands on the stated host letter and codepoint in the candidate text, so no host is misplaced by count. I did not run a script diff of consonants and vowels between baseline and candidate. Spot checks agreed, including מְזֻזוֹת and לְטֹטָפֹת in block 1 and מְזוּזוֹת and לְטוֹטָפֹת in block 3.
